PMID:41492340.setting: Bone and Joint Center ward (88 beds) of a tertiary Class III Grade A general hospital, Henan Provincial People's Hospital, Zhengzhou
PMID:41492340.standard: 10 JBI-style review indicators derived from best evidence on perioperative oral nutritional supplements (ONS) in elderly hip fracture, e.g. staff ONS training (pass ≥80 points), NRS2002 screening within 24 h of admission, 24 h after surgery and before discharge, energy 25–30 kcal/(kg·d) and protein 1.0–1.5 g/kg, ONS 400–600 mL/d after surgery, post-discharge ONS 400 kcal and 30 g protein daily

cycle1.result: Compliance 0–10.7% across the 10 review indicators: staff training 10.7% (3/28); patient/caregiver education, screening, energy/protein targets, ONS use, disease-specific ONS, stopping rule, GI monitoring and discharge follow-up all 0%. Staff knowledge score 61.07±12.36.

PMID:41492340.intervention: Nurse-led multidisciplinary team with nutrition support nurses; daily 20-minute staff training over five days; updated NRS2002 form in the nursing IT system with fixed screening time points and automated reminders; 24-hour dietary energy and protein record sheet; dietary lists, leaflets, education manuals, QR codes, videos and teach-back; ward ONS supply protocol; discharge follow-up manual and smart cloud follow-up platform.

cycle2.result: Compliance 25–100% (all P < 0.05): 100% for indicators 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 and 9; staff training 82.1% (23/28); ONS twice daily after surgery 56.8% (25/44); post-discharge ONS 25.0% (11/44). Staff knowledge score 85.57±16.89 (t = 6.195, P < 0.001).

PMID:41492340.other_findings: Discharge NRS2002 fell from 3.80±0.41 to 2.77±0.42 (P < 0.001) and patients at nutritional risk at discharge fell from 49/49 to 34/44 (P = 0.001); discharge albumin, length of stay and complications did not change significantly. Post-discharge nutritional follow-up stayed poor at 25%.

PMID:35430111.topic: COVID-19 infection and mortality in hip fracture
PMID:35430111.setting: Multicentre collaboration (IMPACT Global Hip Fracture Audit) of 112 hospitals in 14 countries
PMID:35430111.country: Multinational (Australia, Argentina, Chile, Cyprus, England, India, Italy, Greece, Mexico, Northern Ireland, Scotland, Spain, Sudan, Wales)

cycle1.result: 651 (9.2%) patients had COVID-19: 225 (34.6%) positive at presentation and 426 (65.4%) positive postoperatively. 30-day survival 72.7% with COVID-19 versus 92.6% without (p < 0.001); COVID-19 independently associated with 30-day mortality (HR 2.83, p < 0.001).

PMID:35430111.other_findings: Positive COVID-19 status was associated with male sex, residential care, inpatient fall, ASA grade 4–5 and longer admission; length of stay of 10 days or more predicted postoperative COVID-19 (AUC 71.6%). Among COVID-19-positive patients, older age, male sex, renal disease and pulmonary disease predicted 30-day mortality.

PMID:21214946.topic: Pelvic fracture deaths in autopsy-based trauma audit
PMID:21214946.setting: Athens Forensic Medical Department, medico-legal autopsies of fatal falls (Attica Trauma Audit and Research Autopsy-Based Registry)

cycle1.result: 209 (21.5%) of 970 fatal falls had pelvic fracture. Median ISS 50 (17-75) versus 26 (1-75) in controls (p < 0.0001); 163 (78%) potentially preventable deaths (ISS < 75); only 6 (2.9%) deaths directly attributed to pelvic fracture; pre-hospital mortality 70.3% versus 42.7% (p < 0.001).

PMID:21214946.other_findings: 126 (60.3%) of the pelvic fracture group had another injury code denoting major haemorrhage; median post-traumatic survival was 30 minutes versus 20 hours in controls. Psychiatric history had about 300% higher odds in the pelvic fracture group (OR 4.18).

PMID:32616972.topic: Open fracture antibiotic and tetanus prophylaxis
PMID:32616972.setting: Hospital João XXIII (Fundação Hospitalar de Minas Gerais), state public hospital specialised in urgency and trauma, Belo Horizonte
PMID:32616972.standard: Institutional Clinical Protocol 'Primary Treatment of Exposed Fractures' (FHEMIG, 2014): preoperative antibiotics; regimen by Gustilo type (cefazolin 1 g IV 6-hourly ± gentamicin 240 mg daily ± metronidazole 500 mg 6-hourly); duration 24 hours for types I and II and 72 hours for type III; tetanus prophylaxis according to vaccination history

cycle1.result: Preoperative antibiotics prescribed in 221 (91.7%); 59.3% (99/167) received a regimen not recommended by the protocol; 58.0% (254/438) of antibiotic doses were inconsistent; 63.5% of courses had an inadequate duration (95.6% of type I and II given > 24 hours); only 34 (14.1%) patients immunised against tetanus and vaccination history missing in 207 (85.9%).

PMID:32616972.other_findings: Gustilo classification was not recorded in 39.4% of patients; infection occurred in 18.7% and was associated with type III fractures, postoperative antibiotic start and antibiotics started more than 3 hours after admission. Mean time to surgery was 4 hours 12 minutes, with 82.6% operated within 6 hours.

PMID:30294438.setting: The Aga Khan University Hospital, tertiary care academic level-1 trauma hospital, orthopaedic trauma registry

cycle1.result: 177 patients with 189 fractures (113 lower limb, 76 upper limb); 176 (93.1%) had surgery. Radiological outcomes at about 3 months, e.g. radial shaft union excellent in 10/10 (100%), ulnar union excellent in 10/12 (83.3%), distal radius excellent in 3, good in 4 and poor in 1 of 8 assessed.

PMID:30294438.other_findings: Follow-up radiological data were available for only a subset of fractures (e.g. 5 of 13 humeral shaft, 4 of 13 femoral shaft, 14 of 26 tibial shaft). 34 of 47 (72.3%) proximal femur fractures had no in-hospital systemic complication.
